title: First correction to the critical mean degree in extreme long-range percolation
shortTitle: The cost of stepping straight back
oneLine: In one-dimensional long-range percolation, the threshold sits above the branching prediction by a two-step return weight; the same criterion handles summable additions and mixtures of tail exponents.
abstract: For independent undirected bonds on the integers with exact probabilities C|x−y|^(−1−σ), the critical expected degree satisfies pc=1+ζ(2+2σ)/(2ζ(1+σ)²)+O(σ³) as σ decreases to zero. In particular, (pc−1)/σ² tends to π²/12. A positive first-order lace remainder, a nonbacktracking lower bound and uniform Fourier estimates also yield a two-scale kernel criterion, arbitrary bounded-mass nonnegative summable additions, and compact mixtures of exponent ratios. Constants are not evaluated: this is not a numerical threshold estimate at a specified positive exponent.

keyResults: The critical expected degree is 1 plus the exact two-step return weight, with a uniform cubic remainder as the exponent tends to zero.
A reusable two-scale criterion transfers the conclusion to even one-dimensional kernels satisfying the stated Fourier and admissibility assumptions.
Summable positive additions alter the leading coefficient explicitly; compact exponent mixtures replace it by π²/12 times the squared mean exponent ratio.

narration:
Imagine points at every integer along a line. Each pair may be connected, with long connections becoming less likely as their length grows. Percolation asks when these random bonds can form an infinite connected cluster.

This paper studies the limit in which the distance penalty becomes very weak. Its parameter is the expected number of neighbours of a point. A branching approximation suggests that the critical value should approach one. But an undirected connection can take an exploration straight back to the point it just left, without discovering anything new.

The result identifies the first correction above one. It is the two-step return probability of the normalized connection kernel. For the pure power-law model, the correction is pi squared over twelve, multiplied by the square of the small exponent, with an error of cubic order.

The proof combines a lower bound that forbids immediate returns with established lace-expansion machinery and uniform Fourier estimates. The return mechanism itself is familiar from earlier work. The contribution here is control in this fixed, one-dimensional small-exponent regime and extensions to other kernels.

Those extensions show that local connections matter. Adding a fixed amount of nearest-neighbour weight changes the leading coefficient explicitly. Mixing tail exponents in a fixed positive interval gives another formula involving their mean.

These are asymptotic statements. The paper does not evaluate the error constant or give a certified threshold at a chosen positive exponent. It concerns independent, undirected bonds with an exact linear probability law, not every long-range network model. The written proof remains an unrefereed candidate. Internal diagnostic checks are not formal verification or independent confirmation.

This briefing accompanies First correction to the critical mean degree, dated the eleventh of October, twenty twenty-six. The paper and evidence are linked on Evidence Press. The voice is AI-generated, and this briefing is not additional evidence.
